subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures what the city is actually using, street by street.
parts: acoustic leak sensors on water mains

subsystems.name: Communications and edge
subsystems.role: carries the measurements back and runs simple control locally so it survives a network outage.

subsystems.name: Data platform
subsystems.role: turns many utilities' data into one consistent, time-stamped picture.

subsystems.name: Digital twin and forecasting
subsystems.role: a live model of the city's power and water networks that predicts the next few hours.

subsystems.name: Optimisation and control
subsystems.role: decides what to do: shift load, change pressure, charge storage.

subsystems.name: Actuation and operations
subsystems.role: physically changes the network and keeps humans in charge.
parts: building HVAC and EV charge control

buildSteps.title: Map the network
buildSteps.detail: Survey every pipe, cable, substation and valve into an accurate GIS model, recording age, diameter and capacity. Legacy records are usually the hardest part.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the critical nodes
buildSteps.detail: Start where it pays: substations, pumping stations, district meters and the largest consumers. Whole-city per-building sensing comes later.

buildSteps.title: Connect and add edge compute
buildSteps.detail: Build the radio and fibre links, and put local controllers at pumps and substations so they keep working if the central system is unreachable.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the twin
buildSteps.detail: Run the hydraulic and load-flow models against measured pressures and currents until the simulated city matches the real one within a few percent.

buildSteps.title: Add forecasting
buildSteps.detail: Train models on weather, calendar and occupancy data to predict demand hours ahead, and to flag leaks or losses as unusual flow patterns.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop on one sector
buildSteps.detail: Automate a proven win, such as night-time pressure management to cut water losses, or voltage optimisation and demand response on the power side.

buildSteps.title: Couple the sectors
buildSteps.detail: Feed both twins into one optimiser so water pumping, heating, cooling and EV charging use the same cheap, low-carbon hours.

buildSteps.title: Harden and govern
buildSteps.detail: Define fail-safe defaults, segment the network against cyber attack, agree who owns the data, and train operators to trust and override the system.

prerequisites.why: without continuous measurement there is nothing to optimise.
burying sensors citywide is only affordable with long-life, low-bandwidth radio.

prerequisites.tech: Water network and grid automation hardware
prerequisites.why: remote valves, pumps and breakers are the muscles the software commands.
district and single-utility twins are demonstrated, but whole-city coupled twins are not.
power, water, waste and transport are modelled in incompatible formats and owned by different bodies.
centralising control of power and water creates a single high-value target.

pathway.milestone: smart meters, SCADA and district-level leak detection in individual utilities
pathway.unlocks: billions of litres of water and percent-level energy savings in well-run cities.

pathway.milestone: automated sector optimisation: pressure management, voltage control, large-customer demand response
pathway.unlocks: flexible load that helps absorb variable renewables.

pathway.milestone: coupled power–water–heat digital twin running one pilot district in near real time
pathway.unlocks: proof that cross-sector optimisation beats managing each network alone.

pathway.milestone: city-wide orchestration with guaranteed fail-safe operation
pathway.unlocks: much lower losses and a genuine path toward waste-zero operation — though heat and water still cannot be moved cheaply across a whole city.
